tool_args.old_string:
Fine-grained structured pruning of reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs)---removing MLP channel groups rather than entire layers---is typically followed by recovery training (SFT or RLVR) to restore reasoning capabilities.
RLVR is widely considered superior, yet we demonstrate that this hierarchy reflects suboptimal pruning rather than a fundamental property of RL: when pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant (max $|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| {=} 1.34$\,pp across 4 fine-grained criteria and 3 sparsity levels on GSM8K and MBPP, with differences remaining within statistical noise on MATH-500), a phenomenon we term \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}.
We propose Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), which balances gradient importance with CKA-based representational diversity via a coefficient $\alpha$.
A dose-response analysis across $\alpha \in \{0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0\}$ on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B reveals an inverted-U: recovery peaks at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% on GSM8K), the optimal balance of importance and diversity.
Under identical GRPO training, importance-dominated pruning ($\alpha{=}1.0$) collapses while diversity-preserving criteria achieve active learning (peak reward 4.4$\times$ vs Standard), forming a \emph{recovery capacity spectrum} that tracks preserved representational diversity.
Cross-scale (1.5B) and cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) experiments provide initial evidence for generality.

tool_args.old_string:
Reasoning Large Language Models can be compressed through structured pruning, but the pruned model must recover its reasoning capabilities through fine-tuning.
The dominant assumption is that the recovery paradigm---SFT versus RLVR---determines recovery quality: \citet{selfhealing2025} demonstrate that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT.
We show that this hierarchy is an artifact of suboptimal pruning.
When pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant: mean $|\Delta(\text{GRPO}-\text{SFT})| {=} 0.54$\,pp (max $1.14$\,pp) on GSM8K across all fine-grained pruning criteria and sparsity levels; the maximum including MBPP is $1.34$\,pp.
What determines recovery quality is not \emph{how} you train after pruning, but \emph{which structures} you remove during pruning.

Existing structured pruning methods for reasoning LLMs~\citep{graspprune2026,resp2025,llmpruner2023,bonsai2025} optimize for post-pruning quality without studying how the criterion shapes downstream RL recovery.
\citet{rlsqueezes2026} show that RL and SFT impose fundamentally different demands on model representations---RL compresses incorrect paths while SFT expands correct ones---suggesting that pruning decisions should affect RL trainability.
Yet no prior work has compared multiple pruning criteria under RL or asked whether the ``RLVR $>$ SFT'' advantage persists across pruning strategies.
We note that \citet{selfhealing2025} evaluate unstructured magnitude pruning retaining 96.5\% of dense parameters; our findings concern fine-grained structural pruning where entire channel groups are removed, and the two settings may impose different demands on RL recovery.

We design a controlled comparison framework to isolate the effect of pruning criterion on post-RLVR recovery capacity.
The framework consists of three components: (1) shared structural analysis that computes importance and functional overlap scores for all prunable structures, (2) four scoring criteria that combine these scores differently to select structures for removal, and (3) an identical two-stage recovery pipeline applied to all pruned models.
By varying only the scoring criterion while holding all other factors constant, we can attribute differences in GRPO training dynamics directly to the pruning decision.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Structured pruning of LLMs.}
LLM-Pruner~\citep{llmpruner2023} introduced dependency-aware structural pruning for transformers; Bonsai~\citep{bonsai2025} achieves competitive results using only forward passes; GRASPrune~\citep{graspprune2026} advances the state of the art with global gating that jointly prunes FFN channels and KV head groups.
ShortGPT~\citep{shortgpt2024}, SliceGPT~\citep{slicegpt2024}, and LaCo~\citep{yang2024laco} target depth pruning, though \citet{shrestha2026layerpruninglimits} show this causes severe reasoning degradation even when classification is preserved; Wanda~\citep{wanda2024} addresses unstructured sparsity; \citet{doingmore2026} revisit the structured-vs-unstructured trade-off under test-time scaling.
For reasoning models, RESP~\citep{resp2025} uses gradient-based importance on self-generated reasoning traces, RAC~\citep{rac2025} reconstructs chain-of-thought during pruning, SSGR~\citep{ssgr2025} uses self-generated calibration data, and \citet{llms2lrms2026} find width pruning more robust than depth pruning for reasoning but do not study RLVR recovery.
A parallel line recognizes that functional structure should guide pruning: FANG~\citep{fang_2025} groups FFN neurons by activation clusters, FuncNet~\citep{funcnet_2025} decomposes LLMs via ICA, and MPruner~\citep{mpruner2024} uses inter-layer CKA~\citep{kornblith2019cka} for depth pruning in CNNs.
Our work uses \emph{intra-layer} CKA between individual structures at a finer granularity, optimizing for RL recovery capacity rather than immediate accuracy preservation.

\paragraph{Pruning-aware recovery.}
\citet{selfhealing2025} demonstrate that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT, but evaluate only importance-based pruning; our controlled experiments demonstrate that this RLVR${>}$SFT advantage vanishes under diversity-preserving pruning---it is a property of the pruning criterion, not of RL training itself.
We note that our experiments use different models and tasks than \citet{selfhealing2025}; the finding may not transfer to their exact setup.
$P^2$ Law~\citep{p2law2025} establishes scaling laws for post-training loss after pruning.
PASER~\citep{paser2025} optimizes recovery data selection, PAT~\citep{pat2025} jointly considers pruning and fine-tuning objectives, RestoreLCC~\citep{restorelcc_2025} contrastively probes critical attention heads for post-hoc compensation, \citet{boiling_frog_2026} adopt iterative prune-tune loops for gradual compression, and OPSD~\citep{opsd2026} compresses reasoning models \emph{after} RLVR (the reverse of our pipeline).
ARRoL~\citep{xu2026arrol} prunes rollouts during RLVR generation for training efficiency.
These approaches optimize complementary axes; our work isolates which \emph{pruning criterion} enables RL-based recovery.
The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth} asks which subnetworks train effectively from random initialization; our recovery capacity spectrum extends this to \emph{paradigm-conditioned trainability}, where the optimal subnetwork depends on the recovery paradigm (RLVR vs.\ SFT).

\paragraph{RLVR training dynamics.}
\citet{rlsqueezes2026} show that RLVR \emph{compresses} incorrect reasoning trajectories via global exploration, while SFT \emph{expands} correct ones via local imitation---predicting RL--SFT complementarity.
Our results qualify this prediction: the asymmetry manifests as a recovery capacity difference (the spectrum), but the expected accuracy complementarity disappears when pruning preserves representational diversity ($|\Delta| \leq 1.34$\,pp on GSM8K and MBPP; \S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
RL training instability has been studied in the RLHF context: \citet{gao2023overoptimization} characterize reward overoptimization, \citet{dong2025rlplus} document repetitive output collapse during extended RL training, and \citet{shah2025comedy} analyze compounding bias from reward estimation.
\citet{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks} show that RL fine-tuning updates only 5--30\% of parameters, raising the question of whether pruning criteria interact with this active subnetwork.
Our work connects this instability literature to structural pruning, showing that the pruning criterion shapes susceptibility to RL collapse.

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Structured pruning of LLMs.}
Width pruning methods---LLM-Pruner~\citep{llmpruner2023}, Bonsai~\citep{bonsai2025}, GRASPrune~\citep{graspprune2026}---remove attention heads or FFN channels while preserving dense computation.
Depth pruning~\citep{shortgpt2024,slicegpt2024,yang2024laco} removes entire layers but causes severe reasoning degradation~\citep{shrestha2026layerpruninglimits}; \citet{doingmore2026} revisit the trade-off under test-time scaling.
For reasoning models specifically, RESP~\citep{resp2025}, RAC~\citep{rac2025}, and SSGR~\citep{ssgr2025} refine calibration data but retain gradient-based importance as the scoring criterion; \citet{llms2lrms2026} confirm width pruning is more robust than depth pruning for reasoning yet do not study RLVR recovery.
A separate line uses functional structure to guide pruning: FANG~\citep{fang_2025} clusters FFN neurons by activation, FuncNet~\citep{funcnet_2025} decomposes LLMs via ICA, and MPruner~\citep{mpruner2024} applies inter-layer CKA~\citep{kornblith2019cka} for depth pruning in CNNs.
We differ in both granularity and objective: \emph{intra-layer} CKA between individual structures, optimizing for RL recovery capacity rather than immediate accuracy.

\paragraph{Pruning-aware recovery.}
\citet{selfhealing2025} show that RLVR restores pruned reasoning models to near-original accuracy, significantly outperforming SFT---but evaluate only importance-based pruning.
Our controlled experiments show that the RLVR${>}$SFT advantage vanishes under diversity-preserving pruning: it is a property of the pruning criterion, not of RL itself (though our experiments use different models and tasks, so the finding may not transfer to their exact setup).
Other work optimizes complementary axes: $P^2$~Law~\citep{p2law2025} models post-pruning scaling, PASER~\citep{paser2025} selects recovery data, PAT~\citep{pat2025} jointly optimizes pruning and fine-tuning, RestoreLCC~\citep{restorelcc_2025} compensates critical attention heads post hoc, \citet{boiling_frog_2026} iterate prune-tune loops, and OPSD~\citep{opsd2026} compresses reasoning models \emph{after} RLVR.
None of these ask which \emph{pruning criterion} enables RL-based recovery---the question we address.
The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth} asks which subnetworks train effectively from scratch; our recovery capacity spectrum extends this to \emph{paradigm-conditioned trainability}, where the optimal subnetwork depends on the recovery paradigm (RLVR vs.\ SFT).

\paragraph{RLVR training dynamics.}
\citet{rlsqueezes2026} show that RLVR \emph{compresses} incorrect reasoning trajectories while SFT \emph{expands} correct ones, predicting RL--SFT complementarity.
Our results qualify this: the asymmetry manifests as a recovery capacity difference (the spectrum), but the expected accuracy complementarity disappears when pruning preserves representational diversity ($|\Delta| \leq 1.34$\,pp on GSM8K and MBPP; \S\ref{sec:decoupling}).
RL instability is well studied in the RLHF context~\citep{gao2023overoptimization,dong2025rlplus,shah2025comedy}; \citet{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks} find that RL fine-tuning updates only 5--30\% of parameters, raising the question of whether pruning criteria interact with this active subnetwork.
We connect these observations to structural pruning, showing that the criterion shapes susceptibility to RL collapse.

\label{sec:conclusion}

We show that the widely observed RLVR${>}$SFT hierarchy for pruned reasoning models reflects suboptimal fine-grained structural pruning rather than a fundamental property of RL: when pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp, max $1.14$\,pp on GSM8K across all tested fine-grained conditions; $1.34$\,pp including MBPP).

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	The belief that RLVR is inherently superior to SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models turns out to depend on how the model was pruned.
5	Under diversity-preserving pruning, the two recovery paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp on GSM8K, max $1.14$\,pp; $1.34$\,pp including MBPP), while the pruning criterion itself creates a 4.4$\times$ gap in peak reward between CKA-only and Standard---a gap that persists through 300 training steps.
6	Representational diversity is a strong predictor of this recovery capacity: CKA-only diverges most from the dense representation ($\mu{=}0.62$) yet recovers best, while collapsing methods preserve dense fidelity ($\mu{\geq}0.88$), though causal verification remains for future work.
7	
8	Reward-accuracy decoupling is sparsity-dependent.
9	At 15\%, GRPO can still amplify the CKA-only advantage; at 20--25\%, it cannot improve upon SFT baselines, making reward trajectory---not accuracy---the appropriate diagnostic for recovery capacity.
10	Cross-scale (1.5B) and cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) experiments provide initial evidence for generality.
11	
12	Our findings are established for fine-grained structural pruning (MLP channel removal); \citet{selfhealing2025} study unstructured magnitude pruning retaining 96.5\% of parameters, and whether their RLVR${>}$SFT advantage similarly vanishes under diversity-preserving criteria remains open.
13	Whether CKA-based pruning preferentially preserves structures within the active RL subnetwork---\citet{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks} find that only 5--30\% of parameters are updated during RL---is a promising direction for mechanistic explanation.

4	The belief that RLVR is inherently superior to SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models turns out to depend on how the model was pruned.
5	Under diversity-preserving pruning, the two recovery paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp across the four fine-grained criteria at 20\%; max $1.34$\,pp including dose-response variations and MBPP), while the pruning criterion itself creates a 4.4$\times$ gap in peak reward between CKA-only and Standard, a gap that persists through 300 training steps.

20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机

40

42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

Representational diversity is a strong predictor of this recovery capacity: CKA-only diverges most from the dense representation ($\mu{=}0.62$) yet recovers best, while collapsing methods preserve dense fidelity ($\mu{\geq}0.88$), though causal verification remains for future work.

\paragraph{Why does diversity preservation enable RL recovery?}
Policy gradient methods require trajectory variation to estimate reward gradients.
Importance-based pruning collapses the model onto the dense model's dominant reasoning mode, limiting rollout diversity; CKA-only pruning removes functionally redundant structures regardless of gradient importance, preserving representationally distinct pathways that sustain exploration.
Our gradient flow evidence (2.89$\times$ mean magnitude for CKA-only vs Standard; \S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}) is consistent with this account: diverse representations propagate stronger gradients, preventing the zero-variance batches ($f_0 > 0.5$) that characterize collapse.

\paragraph{Connection to RL subnetwork sparsity.}
\citet{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks} find that RL fine-tuning updates only 5--30\% of parameters, implying a small active subnetwork drives RL learning.
If CKA-based pruning preferentially preserves structures within this active subnetwork, by retaining representationally unique components that RL relies on for exploration, it would explain the recovery capacity gap.
Conversely, importance-based pruning may remove structures critical to the RL subnetwork, since gradient importance during forward inference need not correlate with the parameter subset updated during RL.
Verifying this overlap is a promising direction for mechanistic explanation.

\paragraph{Recovery lottery tickets.}
The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth} asks which subnetworks train effectively from scratch.
Our spectrum suggests a \emph{recovery} analogue: CKA-only pruning may identify subnetworks that recover effectively under RL, a form of paradigm-conditioned lottery ticket.
The key distinction is that the same pruned architecture recovers well under both GRPO and SFT (reward-accuracy decoupling), but the reward trajectory reveals whether the subnetwork sustains active RL learning.

\paragraph{Practitioner guidelines.}
When RLVR recovery is planned, prefer CKA-only or high-$\alpha$ \rasp{} ($\alpha \geq 2.0$); the inverted-U (Figure~\ref{fig:dose_response}) shows moderate diversity weighting outperforms both extremes.
When only SFT is available, the criterion still matters (CKA-only exceeds Standard by 4.62\,pp at 20\%) but the margin is smaller than the reward gap suggests.
In either case, maintain per-layer capacity floors ($\geq$40\% retention) and stay below 25\% sparsity to avoid universal collapse (\S\ref{sec:sparsity_cliff}).
Early-step $f_0$ (fraction of zero-variance batches) can serve as a cheap diagnostic for pruning quality before committing to full recovery training.

\paragraph{Scope and outlook.}
Reward-accuracy decoupling is sparsity-dependent: at 15\%, GRPO can still amplify the CKA-only advantage; at 20--25\%, it cannot improve upon SFT baselines, making reward trajectory the appropriate diagnostic for recovery capacity.
Cross-scale (1.5B) and cross-architecture (Qwen2.5-Math-7B, SFT-based recovery) experiments provide initial evidence for generality.
Our findings are established for fine-grained structural pruning (MLP channel removal); \citet{selfhealing2025} study unstructured magnitude pruning retaining 96.5\% of parameters, and whether their RLVR${>}$SFT advantage similarly vanishes under diversity-preserving criteria remains open.
\citet{xu2026arrol} prune rollouts \emph{during} RLVR training; whether their online pruning interacts with the pre-training criterion studied here is a further open question.

Code, pruning masks, and model checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.
